questions.q: How is a getter named `total` referenced inside an LWC template?
options: {total()}  -- with parentheses, like any method call
{total}  -- exactly like a plain property, with no parentheses
{this.total()}
Getters cannot be referenced from a template at all
questions.explain: The template references a getter exactly like a plain property, with no parentheses -- the template has no way to tell (and doesn't need to) whether a bound value comes from a field or a getter.

questions.q: What is the main bug risk this lesson identifies with storing a derived value like `total` in a plain field instead of a getter?
options: Plain fields cannot hold numeric values
You have to remember to recompute and reassign the field everywhere its dependencies change, and missing one spot leaves it silently stale
Plain fields cause a compile-time error when used in a template
Fields render slower than getters in every case
questions.explain: A manually-updated field requires recomputing it at every place its underlying dependencies change -- miss one, and the field goes stale without any error. A getter removes this risk because it's always computed fresh when read.

questions.q: When does the LWC framework actually re-evaluate a getter?
options: Continuously, on a fixed timer, regardless of whether the template re-renders
Only once, the first time the component is created
Whenever the template re-renders and the getter is referenced -- which happens automatically when a reactive field the getter depends on changes
Only when the developer manually calls the getter as a function
questions.explain: A getter is re-evaluated when the template re-renders and references it. Since the framework already re-renders when a dependency changes, a getter effectively 'recomputes automatically' without ever being called like a function.

questions.q: In the `openCases` / `openCaseCount` example, what is the benefit of `openCaseCount` calling the `openCases` getter rather than re-filtering `this.cases` itself?
options: It makes the component deploy faster
It keeps the definition of 'open' in exactly one place, so if that definition changes, every getter and template built on top of `openCases` stays correct automatically
It is required syntax -- a getter cannot read `this.cases` directly
It prevents `openCases` from ever being used directly in a template
questions.explain: Having openCaseCount build on openCases avoids duplicating the filtering logic. If the definition of 'open' changes, there's a single getter to update rather than several places that each independently re-implement the same filter.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when is a plain reactive field still the right choice over a getter?
options: Never -- getters should replace every field in a well-written component
For values set directly by user input, server responses, or wire adapters -- getters are for values derived from that underlying state, not for the state itself
Only for boolean values, never for numbers or strings
Only inside the constructor
questions.explain: Getters are for values derived from other data. The underlying state itself -- what the user typed, what the server returned, what a wire adapter provisioned -- still belongs in a plain reactive field.
